q.zh-Hant: UW MHCI+D 讀多久？學費多少？
q.en: How long is UW MHCI+D, and how much does it cost?

a.zh-Hant: 11 個月全日制，至少 46 學分；學費每學分 1,383 美元，官網估算 63,618 美元，州內外與國際學生同價，另有每學季註冊費、科技費與 U-Pass 等費用。
a.en: It is an 11-month full-time programme of at least 46 credits; tuition is US$1,383 per credit, an estimated US$63,618, the same for residents, non-residents and international students, plus quarterly registration, technology and U-Pass fees.

q.zh-Hant: 雅思、托福要多少分？
q.en: What IELTS or TOEFL score is required?

a.zh-Hant: IELTS 總分 7.5 且口說至少 8.0；TOEFL iBT 2026 年 1 月 21 日起新制 5.0 且口說 5.0，該日前舊制 106 且口說 26；或 Duolingo 135。成績在截止日時須未滿兩年。
a.en: IELTS 7.5 with at least 8.0 in speaking; TOEFL iBT 5.0 with 5.0 speaking for tests from 21 January 2026, or 106 with 26 speaking for earlier tests; or Duolingo 135. Scores must be less than two years old at the deadline.

q.zh-Hant: 一定要交作品集嗎？
q.en: Is a portfolio required?

a.zh-Hant: 要交補充材料：一頁 PDF 附上能展示創造、設計或迭代能力的項目連結（設計作品集、GitHub、研究項目等皆可），以及一支介紹其中一個項目的 1 分鐘影片；作品不要直接上傳到申請系統。
a.en: Supplementary materials are required: a one-page PDF linking to projects that show your ability to create, design or iterate (a design portfolio, GitHub page or research project all work), plus a one-minute video about one of those projects; do not upload the work to the application itself.

q.zh-Hant: 設計或建築背景可以申請嗎？
q.en: Can I apply with a design or architecture background?

a.zh-Hant: 可以。最低條件是學士學位與 GPA 3.0，官網說明更重視你在原本領域中的解題過程，而不是預先做出入學後才會做的作品。
a.en: Yes. The minimum requirements are a bachelor's degree and a 3.0 GPA, and the website says it values your problem-solving process within your own field more than work anticipating what you would do after the programme.

q.zh-Hant: 2027 入學什麼時候截止？何時發榜？
q.en: When is the 2027 deadline, and when are decisions released?

a.zh-Hant: 申請於 2026 年 10 月 1 日開放，2027 年 1 月 18 日截止；錄取與拒絕通知於 3 月中以 email 發出，錄取者約需在 4 月 15 日前回覆。
a.en: Applications opened on 1 October 2026 and close on 18 January 2027; offers and denials are emailed in mid-March, and admitted students reply by around 15 April.

title.en: How to apply to Georgia Tech's MS in Human-Computer Interaction (MS-HCI): 2027 tracks, TOEFL/IELTS, portfolio, tuition and deadline (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 喬治亞理工學院（Georgia Tech）人機交互碩士 MS-HCI 只收秋季入學，每年 2 月 1 日截止。對照官網整理四個學院方向（工業設計、交互計算、LMC、心理學）、四學期 36 學分＋暑期實習＋碩士項目、TOEFL 100／IELTS 7.5 門檻、作品集與 1–2 分鐘影片要求、2026 秋季學費與 GRA／GTA 資助。
summary.en: Georgia Tech's MS in Human-Computer Interaction admits for the autumn only, with a 1 February deadline. Checked against official sources: the four tracks (Industrial Design, Interactive Computing, LMC, Psychology), the four-semester, 36-credit curriculum with a summer internship and master's project, the TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7.5 minimums, the portfolio and one- to two-minute video, Fall 2026 tuition and GRA/GTA funding.

tldr.zh-Hant: Georgia Tech MS-HCI 由工業設計、交互計算、LMC、心理學四學院合辦，申請時擇一方向；四學期 36 學分，含第一學期共同核心課、第一年暑期企業實習、第二年 6 學分碩士項目；每屆約 55–65 人，只收秋季，2 月 1 日美東 23:50 截止，3 月中前發榜；不看 GRE；TOEFL 至少 100、IELTS 至少 7.5（錄取者實際更高）；材料含社群問題、1,000 字個人陳述、作品集（工業設計與 LMC 必交）、1–2 分鐘露臉影片、3 封推薦信與履歷；2026 秋季國際生每學期學費 20,096 美元＋雜費 758 美元；無獎學金，可爭取 GRA／GTA；STEM 課程。
tldr.en: Georgia Tech's MS-HCI is run by four schools (Industrial Design, Interactive Computing, LMC and Psychology), and applicants pick one track. It runs four semesters and 36 credits, with shared first-semester core courses, a corporate internship in the first summer and a six-credit second-year master's project. Classes of about 55 to 65 start in the autumn only; the deadline is 1 February at 11:50 p.m. EST, with offers by mid-March. The GRE is not used. Minimums are TOEFL 100 or IELTS 7.5, though admitted students score higher. Materials include a community question, a 1,000-word statement, a portfolio (required for Industrial Design and LMC), a one- to two-minute on-camera video, three letters and a résumé. Fall 2026 tuition for international students is US$20,096 per semester plus US$758 in fees. There are no scholarships, but GRA/GTA roles are possible, and it is a STEM programme.

body.zh-Hant:
結論先講：喬治亞理工學院（Georgia Tech，亞特蘭大）的 Master of Science in Human-Computer Interaction（MS-HCI，人機交互理學碩士）是一個 四個學期、36 學分的跨領域 STEM 碩士，由工業設計、交互計算（Interactive Computing）、文學傳媒與傳播（LMC）、心理學四個學院合辦，申請時就要選一個學院方向（track）。課程包含第一學期的共同核心課、第一年暑假的企業實習，以及第二年 6 學分的碩士項目。只收秋季入學，每年 2 月 1 日（美東時間 23:50）截止，不考 GRE，但英文門檻高：TOEFL 至少 100 或 IELTS 至少 7.5。工業設計與 LMC 方向必交線上作品集，所有人都要交 1–2 分鐘的露臉影片。學費以 2026 年秋季為例，國際生每學期 20,096 美元，另加每學期 758 美元的必繳雜費。

以下內容於 2026 年 10 月對照 MS-HCI 官網的課程介紹、申請流程、申請條件、國際生、資助、學位要求、職涯發展與常見問題頁，以及 Georgia Tech 出納處（Bursar）公布的學費表查核。早期流傳的學費數字（約 2 萬美元）已改為官網現行的 2026 年秋季費率；無法在官網查到出處的資訊一律刪除。

文首封面是 Georgia Tech 工業設計學院 MS-HCI 介紹頁的主視覺，戴著感測線路的手。圖片來源：喬治亞理工學院工業設計學院官網

Georgia Tech MS-HCI 是什麼樣的碩士？四個方向怎麼選？

官網的定位是同時給學生實務技能與理論基礎，培養能設計、實作並評估下一代人機介面的業界人才，課程從 1996 年開始，校友網絡相當大。學生透過四個參與學院之一入學，所選方向反映你的背景與想專精的領域：

  • Industrial Design（工業設計）：設計背景最常見的選擇；工業設計學院頁面列出的選修方向包括以人為本設計、醫療照護設計、互動產品設計、創意與設計認知、介面原型、互動環境設計、通用設計等。申請者會被問到選擇這個方向的原因。
  • Interactive Computing（交互計算，College of Computing）：偏技術與系統實作。
  • Literature, Media, and Communication（LMC，文學傳媒與傳播）：偏數位媒體、敘事與溝通。
  • Psychology（心理學）：偏認知、人因與使用者研究。

官網說明可以同時申請多個方向，但每個方向要分開送申請；錄取後只會被分到一個方向。每屆入學人數約 55 到 65 人，官網也鼓勵有工作經驗、背景多元的人申請。

MS-HCI 要修哪些課？實習與碩士項目怎麼安排？

  • 36 學分、四個學期：包含必修核心課（設計、使用者研究、專業實務），所屬方向的專業選修，以及全校相關課程的一般選修。所有新生第一學期一起修同樣的三門核心課。
  • 成績門檻：總 GPA 至少 3.0；核心課、專業課與項目學分每門至少 B，一般選修至少 C。
  • 暑期實習：所有學生都應在第二與第三學期之間的暑假完成一份 HCI 相關的企業實習；實習要自己找，但課程會協助履歷與作品集準備、公開演講與模擬面試，並分享職缺。
  • 碩士項目（Master’s Project）：第二年在一位 MS-HCI 教師指導下完成 6 學分的項目，可能與企業夥伴合作；第一年春季末提交提案，畢業學期末寫報告並向課程主任、四個學院的教師代表與同學發表。研究項目頁說明這是橫跨兩個學期的項目，常與業界、社區或非營利組織合作。
  • 職涯準備：必修的 Professional Practice and Preparation 課程教履歷與作品集、公開演講與談判，並安排與業界人士一對一的模擬面試；每年春季另有研究成果展 Interactivity@GT。

申請條件是什麼？托福、雅思要多少？

  • 學歷：需四年制學士學位；三年制學士要先聯絡 Georgia Tech 研究生教育處。已有碩士學位也可以申請。
  • GPA：期望本科累積 GPA 3.0 以上，但低於此分數不會自動被拒，審查採整體評估。
  • GRE：不要求、也不列入考量，請不要送分數。
  • 英文：只接受 TOEFL 或 IELTS（其他考試不能替代）。MS-HCI 的最低要求是 TOEFL 100、IELTS 7.5，高於 Georgia Tech 全校標準；官網也說近年錄取者的分數明顯更高，申請條件頁提到近年錄取者的 TOEFL 最低約 110，常見問題頁則寫錄取者最低接近 108、IELTS 接近 8 或以上。在美國大學就讀滿一學年（兩個學期或三個學季）的國際生可豁免。送分代碼使用 Georgia Tech 的 5248。

要交作品集嗎？申請材料有哪些？

  1. 社群問題：說明你的經驗、技能、嗜好與熱情如何讓你積極參與 MS-HCI 社群。
  2. 個人陳述（上限 1,000 字）：學術與研究背景、職涯目標、特別感興趣的領域，以及 Georgia Tech 能如何幫你達成目標；工業設計方向要另外說明為什麼選這個方向。
  3. 作品集：LMC 與工業設計方向必交線上作品集；交互計算方向鼓勵但不強制；心理學方向不要求。官網偏好提供網址，PDF 也可以。
  4. 影片（1–2 分鐘）：用來評估溝通能力並認識你。唯一要求是全程露臉、用自己的聲音說話；內容自由，但建議不要重複個人陳述。偏好用 YouTube 等影片網站的連結。
  5. 3 封推薦信：系統會直接寄信給推薦人。剛畢業的人可考慮兩位教師加一位相關實習主管；已工作的人可找能完整評估你能力的主管或專業人士；親屬、下屬與同儕通常不合適。
  6. 履歷：官網強烈建議附上。

官網說明提早送件沒有優勢，審查要等截止日後才開始；錄取通知通常在 3 月中前由研究生處寄出，拒絕信較晚，部分年份會依錄取者回覆情況進行小規模的第二輪錄取。截止日沒有彈性。

學費多少？國際生有獎學金嗎？

  • 學費：MS-HCI 屬 Georgia Tech 的專業學位課程，在一般研究所學費之上另加附加學費。以出納處公布的 2026 年秋季費率為例，修 12 學分以上每學期：州外國際生（Out of Country）20,096 美元、州外美國學生 19,530 美元、喬治亞州居民 8,315 美元；另有每學期 758 美元的必繳學生雜費（4 學分以上）。下一學年的費率每年春季（通常 5 月）才公布，而且常會調漲，2027 年入學前請以出納處最新費率為準。
  • 修課量：F-1 簽證的國際生每學期須修滿 12 學分，最後一學期可申請降到 6 學分；不能讀非全日制。
  • 資助：課程不提供獎學金，國際生也不符合財務資助資格；但可在後面的學期爭取研究助理（GRA）或教學助理（GTA），提供 12 學分的基本學費減免與月薪，但不包含雜費與 MS-HCI 的附加學費。GRA 每週約工作 15 到 20 小時；第一學期幾乎不可能拿到 GTA，通常要在第一年把課修到 A。
  • STEM：官網常見問題頁確認 MS-HCI 是 STEM 課程。

畢業生去哪裡？

官網列出的常見職稱包括 UX 研究員、UX 設計師、前端工程師、內容策略與產品經理等，雇主從大型跨國科技公司、設計工作室、醫療機構、政府單位到遊戲公司都有，也有畢業生繼續攻讀博士。官網另有歷年實習與就業報告可查。2026 年，MS-HCI 也獲得喬治亞大學系統董事會頒發的系所教學卓越獎。

2027 申請時間線怎麼排？

  • 2026 年 10 月至 12 月：決定方向（設計背景多選工業設計），整理線上作品集，準備 TOEFL 100 或 IELTS 7.5 以上的成績。
  • 2027 年 1 月：完成 1,000 字個人陳述、社群問題、1–2 分鐘露臉影片，確認 3 位推薦人已收到邀請。
  • 2027 年 2 月 1 日（美東時間 23:50）：依官網規則的秋季入學截止日。
  • 2027 年 3 月中前：通常寄出錄取通知；2027 年 8 月秋季開學。

設計、建築背景怎麼準備最有利？

作者建議（非官方要求）：工業設計方向必交作品集，但它看的是 HCI 的思考方式，而不是單純的造型或渲染。我們在 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢中看到，空間或產品設計背景轉 HCI 時，最有說服力的作品集通常會挑 2 到 3 個項目，清楚交代問題怎麼定義、做了哪些使用者研究、草模與原型如何根據測試修改，正好對應官網列出的課程項目目標：定義問題、研究、分析、迭代原型、驗證與溝通。那支 1–2 分鐘影片則建議講個人陳述沒寫到的故事，讓審查者看到你的表達與個性。TOEFL 100 只是最低門檻，建議把目標放在 108 以上。想比較其他 HCI 與娛樂科技碩士，可參考我們的 CMU 人機交互碩士 MHCI 申請整理、華盛頓大學 MHCI+D 申請整理、加州大學爾灣分校 MHCID 申請整理 與 CMU 娛樂科技碩士 ETC 申請整理。

官方查核來源：MS-HCI 首頁、課程介紹、申請流程、申請條件、國際生、資助、學位要求、職涯發展、常見問題、Georgia Tech 出納處學費表、工業設計學院 MS-HCI 頁（2026 年 10 月查核）。
body.en:
The short answer: Georgia Tech's Master of Science in Human-Computer Interaction (MS-HCI) in Atlanta is a four-semester, 36-credit interdisciplinary STEM master's run jointly by four schools: Industrial Design, Interactive Computing, Literature, Media, and Communication (LMC) and Psychology. You choose one of these tracks when you apply. The programme combines shared core courses in the first semester, a corporate internship in the summer after the first year and a six-credit master's project in the second year. It admits for the autumn (fall) semester only, with a deadline of 1 February at 11:50 p.m. EST each year. The GRE is not used, but the English bar is high: TOEFL 100 or IELTS 7.5 at minimum. The Industrial Design and LMC tracks require an online portfolio, and every applicant submits a one- to two-minute on-camera video. Using the Fall 2026 rates, tuition for international students is US$20,096 per semester, plus US$758 per semester in mandatory fees.

Everything below was checked in October 2026 against the MS-HCI website's overview, admissions process, admissions requirements, international students, funding, degree requirements, career outcomes and FAQ pages, and against the tuition tables published by Georgia Tech's Office of the Bursar. Earlier tuition figures in circulation (around US$20,000) have been replaced with the current Fall 2026 rates, and any information without an official source has been removed.

The cover is the banner image from the MS-HCI page of Georgia Tech's School of Industrial Design: a hand wired with sensor leads. Image source: Georgia Tech School of Industrial Design website

What kind of master's is Georgia Tech's MS-HCI, and how do you choose a track?

The website describes a programme that gives students both practical skills and theoretical knowledge, preparing industry leaders in the design, implementation and evaluation of the next generation of human-computer interfaces. It dates back to 1996 and has a large alumni network. Students enter through one of the four participating schools, and the choice reflects their background and intended specialisation:

  • Industrial Design: the most common choice for design graduates. The School of Industrial Design lists elective areas such as human-centred design, health care design, interactive product design, creativity and design cognition, interface prototyping, design of interactive environments and universal design. Applicants are asked why they chose this track.
  • Interactive Computing (College of Computing): more technical and systems-oriented.
  • Literature, Media, and Communication (LMC): leaning towards digital media, narrative and communication.
  • Psychology: leaning towards cognition, human factors and user research.

You may apply to more than one track, but each requires a separate application, and an admitted student is assigned to only one. Entering classes range from 55 to 65 students, and the programme encourages applicants with varied backgrounds, including work experience.

What do MS-HCI students study, and how do the internship and master's project work?

  • 36 credits over four semesters: required core courses (design, user research and professional practice), electives from your track and general electives from across campus. All entering students take the same three core courses together in their first semester.
  • Grade requirements: an overall GPA of at least 3.0, at least a B in core, specialisation and project credits, and at least a C in general electives.
  • Summer internship: all students are expected to complete an HCI-relevant corporate internship in the summer between their second and third semesters. Students find their own placements, but the programme helps with résumés and portfolios, public speaking, mock interviews and job postings.
  • Master's project: a six-credit project in the second year, supervised by an MS-HCI faculty member and possibly with a corporate partner. Students submit a proposal late in the spring of their first year, then write a report and present to the programme directors, the four school coordinators and fellow students late in their final semester. The projects page describes it as a two-semester effort, often in collaboration with industry, communities or non-profits.
  • Career preparation: the required Professional Practice and Preparation course covers résumés, portfolios, public speaking and negotiation, with one-to-one mock interviews with HCI professionals. Interactivity@GT, an annual research showcase, takes place each spring.

What are the entry requirements, and what TOEFL or IELTS score do you need?

  • Degree: a four-year bachelor's degree is required; holders of three-year degrees should contact Georgia Tech's Office of Graduate Education. Applicants who already hold a master's degree may apply.
  • GPA: a cumulative undergraduate GPA of 3.0 or above is expected, but a lower GPA does not mean automatic rejection; reviewers look at the whole application.
  • GRE: neither required nor considered; do not submit scores.
  • English: only TOEFL or IELTS are accepted. The MS-HCI minimums are TOEFL 100 and IELTS 7.5, higher than Georgia Tech's general requirement, and the website says admitted students in recent years have scored much higher: the requirements page mentions a recent TOEFL minimum among admitted students of about 110, while the FAQ says closer to 108, with IELTS closer to 8 or above. International students who have attended a US college or university for at least one academic year (two semesters or three quarters) are exempt. Use Georgia Tech's institution code, 5248.

Is a portfolio required, and what materials do you submit?

  1. Community question: how your experiences, skills, hobbies and passions prepare you to take an active part in the MS-HCI community.
  2. Personal statement (up to 1,000 words): your academic and research background, career goals, special areas of interest and how Georgia Tech will help you reach your objectives. Industrial Design applicants also explain why they chose that track.
  3. Portfolio: an online portfolio is required for LMC and Industrial Design, encouraged but not required for Interactive Computing, and not required for Psychology. A URL is preferred, though a PDF is acceptable.
  4. Video (one to two minutes): used to assess your communication skills and get to know you. The only rule is to be on camera the whole time, speaking in your own voice. The content is up to you, but avoid repeating your statement. A link from a site such as YouTube is preferred.
  5. Three letters of recommendation: the system contacts your recommenders directly. Recent graduates might ask two faculty members and a relevant internship supervisor; working applicants can turn to supervisors or professionals who know their abilities well. Relatives, direct reports and peers are generally not appropriate.
  6. Résumé: strongly recommended.

Applying early brings no advantage, since review begins only after the deadline. Offers are typically sent by mid-March through the Graduate Office, with rejection letters later, and in some years a small second round follows depending on how admitted students respond. The deadline is not flexible.

How much does it cost, and is there funding for international students?

  • Tuition: MS-HCI is a professional degree programme at Georgia Tech, so a supplement is added to standard graduate tuition. Using the Bursar's Fall 2026 rates for 12 or more credits, tuition per semester is US$20,096 for out-of-country students, US$19,530 for out-of-state US students and US$8,315 for Georgia residents, plus US$758 per semester in mandatory student fees (four or more credits). Rates for the next academic year are set each spring, usually in May, and often rise, so check the Bursar's latest table before you enrol in 2027.
  • Course load: international students on F-1 visas must take at least 12 credits each semester and may petition for as few as six in their final semester; part-time study is not possible.
  • Funding: the programme offers no scholarships, and international students are not eligible for financial aid. In later semesters, however, students can seek Graduate Research Assistant (GRA) or Graduate Teaching Assistant (GTA) roles, which carry a 12-credit waiver of base tuition and a monthly stipend, but not mandatory fees or the MS-HCI tuition supplement. GRAs work about 15 to 20 hours a week; GTAs are almost never available in the first semester and usually require an A in the course during the first year.
  • STEM: the FAQ confirms that MS-HCI is a STEM programme.

Where do graduates go?

Typical job titles listed on the website include UX researcher, UX designer, front-end developer, content strategist and product manager. Employers range from large multinational technology firms and design studios to health care organisations, government agencies and game developers, and some graduates go on to PhDs. The website also publishes internship and placement reports. In 2026 the programme received the Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia's Teaching Excellence Award for a department or programme.

How should you plan a 2027 application?

  • October to December 2026: choose your track (design graduates usually pick Industrial Design), build your online portfolio and secure a TOEFL score of 100 or IELTS 7.5 or above.
  • January 2027: finish the 1,000-word statement, the community question and the one- to two-minute video, and make sure your three recommenders have received their invitations.
  • 1 February 2027 (11:50 p.m. EST): the autumn deadline under the programme's stated rule.
  • By mid-March 2027: offers are typically sent; the autumn semester starts in August 2027.

How can design and architecture graduates prepare?

Author's advice (not an official requirement): the Industrial Design track requires a portfolio, but it is looking for HCI thinking rather than form-making or renderings alone. In 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, we have found that the most convincing portfolios from spatial or product designers moving into HCI choose two or three projects and show clearly how the problem was defined, what user research was done and how sketch models and prototypes changed after testing. That mirrors the course-project goals the website lists: define a problem, research, analyse, iterate prototypes, validate and communicate. Use the one- to two-minute video for a story your statement does not tell, so reviewers can see how you express yourself. TOEFL 100 is only the minimum; aim for 108 or above. To compare other HCI and entertainment-technology master's programmes, see our guides to CMU's MHCI, the University of Washington's MHCI+D, UC Irvine's MHCID and CMU's ETC.

Official sources checked: MS-HCI home, overview, admissions process, admissions requirements, international students, funding, degree requirements, career outcomes, FAQ, Georgia Tech Bursar tuition tables and the School of Industrial Design's MS-HCI page (checked October 2026).

q.zh-Hant: Georgia Tech MS-HCI 讀多久？學費多少？
q.en: How long is Georgia Tech's MS-HCI, and how much does it cost?

a.zh-Hant: 四個學期、36 學分，中間第一年暑假要做企業實習。以 2026 年秋季費率，國際生修 12 學分以上每學期學費 20,096 美元，另加每學期 758 美元必繳雜費；費率每年春季公布且常調漲。
a.en: It runs four semesters and 36 credits, with a corporate internship in the summer after the first year. At Fall 2026 rates, international students taking 12 or more credits pay US$20,096 in tuition per semester plus US$758 in mandatory fees; rates are set each spring and often rise.

q.zh-Hant: 托福、雅思要多少分？要考 GRE 嗎？
q.en: What TOEFL or IELTS score is required, and is the GRE needed?

a.zh-Hant: 最低 TOEFL 100 或 IELTS 7.5，只接受這兩種考試，官網說錄取者實際分數更高（TOEFL 約 108–110、IELTS 約 8）。GRE 不要求、也不列入考量。
a.en: The minimums are TOEFL 100 or IELTS 7.5, and only these two tests are accepted; the website says admitted students score higher (TOEFL around 108 to 110, IELTS around 8). The GRE is neither required nor considered.

q.zh-Hant: 一定要交作品集嗎？
q.en: Is a portfolio required?

a.zh-Hant: 看方向：工業設計與 LMC 必交線上作品集，交互計算鼓勵但不強制，心理學不要求。所有方向都要交 1–2 分鐘、全程露臉的影片。
a.en: It depends on the track: Industrial Design and LMC require an online portfolio, Interactive Computing encourages one and Psychology does not require one. Every track requires a one- to two-minute video with you on camera throughout.

q.zh-Hant: 設計或建築背景適合哪個方向？
q.en: Which track suits a design or architecture background?

a.zh-Hant: 多數設計背景會選工業設計方向，選修涵蓋以人為本設計、互動產品、介面原型與互動環境設計；可以同時申請多個方向，但每個要分開送件，錄取後只會分到一個。
a.en: Most design graduates choose the Industrial Design track, whose electives cover human-centred design, interactive products, interface prototyping and interactive environments. You may apply to several tracks, but each needs its own application and you will be assigned to only one.

q.zh-Hant: 2027 入學什麼時候截止？何時發榜？
q.en: When is the 2027 deadline, and when are decisions released?

a.zh-Hant: 只收秋季入學，依官網規則 2 月 1 日美東時間 23:50 截止且沒有彈性；審查在截止後才開始，錄取通知通常在 3 月中前寄出。
a.en: Entry is in the autumn only; under the stated rule the deadline is 1 February at 11:50 p.m. EST and is not flexible. Review begins after the deadline, and offers are typically sent by mid-March.

title.en: How to apply to UC Irvine's Master of Human-Computer Interaction and Design (MHCID): 2027 format, TOEFL/IELTS, portfolio, fees and visa limits (checked October 2026)

summary.zh-Hant: 加州大學爾灣分校（UC Irvine）人機交互與設計碩士 MHCID 是給在職 UX 人士的一年制低駐校碩士，2027 秋季入學 5 月 15 日截止。對照官網整理線上＋三次回校的上課方式、48 學分課程與 Capstone、TOEFL 80／IELTS 7 門檻、作品集或 GRE 二選一、約 6 萬美元學費，以及無法簽發 I-20 的國際生限制。
summary.en: UC Irvine's Master of Human-Computer Interaction and Design is a one-year, low-residency master's for working UX professionals, with a 15 May 2027 deadline for Fall 2027. Checked against official sources: the online-plus-three-visits format, the 48-unit curriculum and capstone, TOEFL 80 / IELTS 7 minimums, the portfolio-or-GRE option, fees of about US$60,000 and the fact that no I-20 can be issued.

tldr.zh-Hant: UCI MHCID 由信息與計算機科學學院信息學系開設，是給在職人士的一年制專業碩士；低駐校混合制，大部分線上，整年回校三次（9 月密集課、3 月春季密集課與 Capstone 啟動、隔年 9 月畢業典禮），但仍是每週 35–40 小時的全日制課程；48 學分＝九門核心課＋三個學季業界專題，最後六個月 4–6 人一組與外部客戶做 Capstone 項目；只收秋季，2027 秋季入學 2027 年 5 月 15 日截止；四年制學士、GPA 3.0、TOEFL 80 或 IELTS 7（單項 6）；目的陳述、履歷、3 封推薦信、作品集或 GRE 二選一（強烈建議作品集 3–4 件附摘要頁）；2026 秋季入學總費用 60,060 美元（四學季各 15,015 美元）；STEM 但無法簽發 I-20，不能辦 F-1 學生簽證。
tldr.en: UCI's MHCID, offered by the Department of Informatics in the School of Information and Computer Sciences, is a one-year professional master's for working people. It is low-residency, mostly online with three campus visits (a September intensive, a March Spring Intensive and capstone kickoff, and commencement the following September), yet it is still a full-time programme of 35 to 40 hours a week. Its 48 units comprise nine core courses and three quarters of industry topics, ending with a six-month capstone in teams of four to six with an external client. Entry is in the autumn only, with a 15 May 2027 deadline for Fall 2027. Requirements: a four-year bachelor's, GPA 3.0, TOEFL 80 or IELTS 7 (bands of 6), a statement of purpose, résumé, three letters and a portfolio or GRE (a portfolio of three or four pieces with summary pages is strongly recommended). Fees for the Fall 2026 cohort total US$60,060 (US$15,015 per quarter for four quarters). It is a STEM degree, but no I-20 can be issued, so it cannot be used for an F-1 student visa.

body.zh-Hant:
結論先講：加州大學爾灣分校（UC Irvine，UCI）的 Master of Human-Computer Interaction and Design（MHCID，人機交互與設計碩士）是信息與計算機科學學院（Donald Bren School of ICS）信息學系開設的 一年制專業碩士，對象是已有工作經驗、想在 UX 領域往上走的在職人士。它採 「低駐校」混合制：大部分課程線上進行，整年只需回爾灣校園三次（9 月開學密集課、3 月春季密集課與 Capstone 啟動、隔年 9 月畢業典禮）。只收秋季入學，2027 年秋季入學的截止日是 2027 年 5 月 15 日；英文門檻是 TOEFL 80 或 IELTS 7（單項不低於 6）；作品集與 GRE 二選一，官網強烈建議交作品集。以 2026 年秋季入學的學費表，總費用約 60,060 美元。最需要注意的是：因為是低駐校課程，官網明說無法簽發 I-20，不能用這個課程申請 F-1 學生簽證，國際申請者一定要先確認自己的簽證與上課方式。

以下內容於 2026 年 10 月對照 MHCID 官網的課程介紹、申請、作品集、課程、Capstone、職涯與常見問題頁，以及 UCI 2026–27 課程目錄、註冊處學費表與研究生院英文要求查核。早期流傳的學費數字（約 3.4 萬美元）已改為官網現行費用；無法在官網查到出處的資訊一律刪除。

文首封面是 MHCID 課程頁的主視覺：一群人圍著桌面上的手機介面線框圖、便利貼與設計思考流程圖討論。圖片來源：加州大學爾灣分校 MHCID 官網

UCI MHCID 是什麼樣的碩士？適合誰讀？

官網的定位很清楚：這是一個給科技業在職人士的專業碩士，特別是已經在 UX 或相關領域工作、想累積專業並成為以人為本設計領導者的人；有工作經驗的應屆畢業生也歡迎申請。2026–27 課程目錄也寫明，任何科系背景都可申請，但通常優先考慮技術、社會科學或設計背景，以及有工作經驗的申請者。

一年內要學的內容包括：人類行為與認知理論、高低保真原型、UX 在軟體開發流程中的位置、實證研究方法與分析、建立人物誌（persona）、情境與故事板的發想與設計流程，以及與客戶和團隊溝通。官網常見問題頁也直接比較了 bootcamp 與碩士：碩士要學的是理論、工具與研究流程背後的基礎，而不只是做出作品集。

如果你想走學術研究路線，官網建議改申請 UCI 的 M.S. Informatics；MHCID 是給想做業界 UX 的人。

上課方式怎麼安排？要讀多久、修哪些課？

  • 低駐校混合制：大部分課程線上完成，整年回校三次：9 月初第一門課 IN4MATX 280 的線下密集課（另有多天的線上部分）、3 月下旬的春季密集課與 Capstone 啟動，以及隔年 9 月的畢業典禮。官網建議 9 月密集課那一週不要安排任何工作。
  • 全日制強度：雖然官網說幾乎所有學生都邊工作邊讀，但這仍是全日制課程，平均每週要投入 35 到 40 小時。
  • 同步進度（lock-step）：全班同時修同樣的課，形成緊密的同屆網絡。每門課都由教師授課，並有多位助教支援。
  • 48 學分、約 12 個月：九門核心課 IN4MATX 280–288（HCI 與設計概論、使用者需求分析、設計與原型、UX 評估、進階設計與原型、互動科技工作室、HCI 與設計創新、兩門 Capstone 項目與作品集課），加上三個學季的 IN4MATX 289 業界應用專題。全程 GPA 須維持 3.0，單科不得低於 B-；正常約 12 個月完成，特殊情況最長 24 個月。
  • 畢業考核：包含 Capstone 項目表現、團隊內個人與同儕互評，以及一份完成的作品集。

Capstone 項目做什麼？

Capstone 項目在課程的最後六個月進行，4 到 6 人一組，和一個外部客戶合作，創新、改善或調整一個新的或既有的數位產品或服務，領域涵蓋教育、環境、醫療、零售等。官網列出的過往客戶包括 Discovery Cube 博物館、蒙特雷灣水族館（Monterey Bay Aquarium）、Data for Social Good、Code.org，以及多家營利企業。官網強調，迭代的研究、設計、開發與評估是 Capstone 成功的關鍵。

申請條件是什麼？托福、雅思要多少？

  • 學歷：需美國區域認證大學或同等的國際學士學位，只接受四年制學士，不接受三年制。
  • GPA：最低 3.0（4.0 制）。
  • 英文：依 UCI 研究生院規定，TOEFL 總分至少 80（2026 年 1 月起的新制為 4 分），或 IELTS 學術組總分至少 7、單項不低於 6；成績須在兩年內，TOEFL 送分代碼 4859，不接受 MyBest。若學士或碩士就讀於依 WHED 資料庫認定以英語為唯一授課語言的學校，可豁免。
  • 材料：線上申請表、目的陳述（為什麼想讀、與職涯規劃的關係、未來目標）、履歷、3 封推薦信（官網說明通常可以、也應該找工作上的主管、同事或客戶）、所有就讀過大學的非正式成績單，以及作品集或 GRE 二選一（強烈建議作品集）；個人經歷陳述（Personal History Statement）為選填。

作品集要怎麼準備？

官網說明，只要交出合格的作品集就可以免 GRE，而且他們認為作品集比 GRE 更能預測學生在課程中的表現。MHCID 的作品集不限設計作品，任何工作領域的成果都可以，重點是展現：良好的寫作能力、對電腦與科技的熟悉度，以及你在本行的實力。

  • 數量：3 到 4 件最能代表你的作品；如果只有 2 到 3 件強項，就不要硬塞較弱的作品湊數。
  • 每件附摘要頁：說明作品內容、用到的技能、帶來的成果，以及你在其中扮演的角色。
  • 格式：個人網站或 PDF；網站連結要放在目的陳述或履歷裡，PDF 可直接上傳。涉及保密的工作內容可以適度遮蔽（例如前雇主的財務細節）。

學費多少？國際生可以申請嗎？

  • 學費：MHCID 是自籌經費的專業課程。依 UCI 註冊處公布、2026 年秋季入學的費用表，項目費（Program Fee）共 59,940 美元，加上每學季 30 美元的學生服務費，四個學季（秋、冬、春、夏）每季 15,015 美元，合計 60,060 美元；另有可選擇退出的 UCGPC 費用 7 美元。官網說明這已包含課程所有費用，但不含回校三次的交通與書籍；費用每年可能調整，2027 年入學請以註冊處最新費用表為準。
  • 訂位金與保險：錄取後需繳 500 美元訂位金（SIR），入學後折抵第一學季費用；課程不提供、也不強制研究生健康保險（GSHIP）。
  • 獎學金：執行委員會會同時審查入學與個別獎學金（fellowship），會盡量與錄取通知一起公布，但有時會延後。因為不是州政府資助的課程，申請費減免可能不適用。
  • 國際生與簽證：官網歡迎國際申請者，也確認 MHCID 屬 STEM 學位，但因為是低駐校課程（一次不需在校超過一週），無法簽發 I-20，課程也不協助辦理學生簽證。已經以非學生簽證（如家屬、工作）身分在美國的人，通常可以就讀，但官網建議先向 UCI 國際中心與移民律師確認。人在台灣、需要回校上密集課的申請者，務必在申請前先問清楚入境與上課的安排。

畢業生去哪裡工作？

官網列出的校友職稱包括 UX 設計師、UX 研究員、平面設計師、產品設計師、內容設計師、產品經理、UX 寫手與 UI 無障礙工程師；任職公司包括 Google、Microsoft、Meta、Apple、Amazon、LinkedIn、Zoom、Oracle、Intel、Boeing、Medtronic、Johnson & Johnson、LEGO BrickLink 等。課程也提供個人化學術輔導，以及工作坊、教練與交流活動等職涯支援。和所有加州大學碩士一樣，MHCID 經 WSCUC 認證。

2027 申請時間線怎麼排？

  • 2026 年 11 月至 2027 年 1 月：先確認自己的簽證身分能否就讀（無 I-20）；整理 3 到 4 件作品與摘要頁，準備 TOEFL 80 或 IELTS 7（單項 6）以上的成績。
  • 2027 年 2 月至 4 月：完成目的陳述與履歷，邀請 3 位推薦人（工作主管、同事或客戶都可以）。官網鼓勵不要拖到最後一刻送件。
  • 2027 年 5 月 15 日：2027 年秋季入學截止日。
  • 2027 年夏天：錄取後繳 500 美元訂位金，收到閱讀清單就開始讀；9 月初回校參加 IN4MATX 280 密集課。

設計、建築背景怎麼準備最有利？

作者建議（非官方要求）：MHCID 看重的是工作經驗與 UX 思考，而不是漂亮的渲染。我們在 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢中看到，空間設計背景的人轉 UX 時，最有說服力的作品通常是把一個實際做過的設計項目重新整理成「使用者是誰、問題怎麼定義、做了哪些研究、方案怎麼根據回饋修改」的流程，並在摘要頁寫清楚自己的角色與成果，這正好對應官網要求的寫作能力、科技熟悉度與專業實力。如果你需要 F-1 簽證到美國全職就讀，MHCID 並不適合，可以比較我們整理的 CMU 人機交互碩士 MHCI、華盛頓大學 MHCI+D、喬治亞理工學院 MS-HCI 與 CMU 娛樂科技碩士 ETC。

官方查核來源：MHCID 首頁、課程介紹、申請、申請作品集、課程、Capstone 項目、職涯發展、常見問題、UCI 2026–27 課程目錄、UCI 註冊處 MHCID 費用表、UCI 研究生院英文要求（2026 年 10 月查核）。
body.en:
The short answer: UC Irvine's Master of Human-Computer Interaction and Design (MHCID) is a one-year professional master's offered by the Department of Informatics in the Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences, aimed at people already working who want to move up in UX. It is low-residency: most teaching is online, and students come to the Irvine campus only three times (an intensive at the start in September, a Spring Intensive and capstone kickoff in March, and commencement the following September). It admits for the autumn (fall) only, and the deadline for Fall 2027 entry is 15 May 2027. The English minimums are TOEFL 80 or IELTS 7 (no band below 6), and you submit either a portfolio or GRE scores, with a portfolio strongly recommended. Based on the fee schedule for the cohort entering in Fall 2026, total fees are about US$60,060. The key caveat: because the programme is low-residency, the website says it cannot issue I-20s, so it cannot be used to obtain an F-1 student visa, and international applicants must check their visa situation and how they will attend before applying.

Everything below was checked in October 2026 against the MHCID website's overview, admissions, portfolio, curriculum, capstone, career and FAQ pages, as well as the UCI 2026–27 catalogue, the Registrar's fee schedule and the Graduate Division's English requirements. An earlier tuition figure in circulation (around US$34,000) has been replaced with current official fees, and any information without an official source has been removed.

The cover is the banner image from the MHCID curriculum page: a group gathered around phone-interface wireframes, sticky notes and a design-thinking diagram on a table. Image source: UC Irvine MHCID website

What kind of master's is UCI's MHCID, and who is it for?

The website is clear about its audience: technology professionals, especially those with experience in user experience or related fields who want to deepen their expertise and grow as leaders in human-centred design; recent graduates with professional experience are also welcome. The 2026–27 catalogue says applicants may hold degrees in any field, though preference generally goes to those with a technical, social-science or design background and work experience.

Over the year, students learn theories of human behaviour and cognition, high- and low-fidelity prototyping, the place of UX in the software development life cycle, empirical methods and analysis, ideation and design processes for personas, scenarios and storyboards, and communication with clients and teams. The FAQ even compares a bootcamp with a master's degree: the degree teaches the fundamentals behind the theories, tools and research processes, not just portfolio pieces.

If you want an academic research path, the website suggests applying to UCI's M.S. in Informatics instead; MHCID is for people heading into professional UX roles.

How is the programme delivered, and what do you study?

  • Low-residency format: most coursework is online, with three campus visits: an in-person intensive in early September for the first course, IN4MATX 280 (which also has a multi-day online portion), a Spring Intensive and capstone kickoff in late March, and commencement the following September. The website advises planning nothing else during the September intensive week.
  • Full-time workload: the website says nearly all students work full-time while studying, but it is still a full-time programme requiring an average of 35 to 40 hours a week.
  • Lock-step cohort: all students take the same classes at the same time, building strong ties. Every class is taught by a faculty member, with support from several teaching assistants.
  • 48 units in about 12 months: nine core courses, IN4MATX 280 to 288 (an overview of HCI and design, user needs analysis, design and prototyping, UX evaluation, advanced design and prototyping, an interactive technology studio, innovations in HCI and design, and two capstone and portfolio courses), plus three quarters of IN4MATX 289 on applying HCI and design in industry. Students must keep a GPA of 3.0 with no grade below B-; normal progress takes about 12 months, with 24 months the maximum by exception.
  • Final assessment: capstone performance, individual and peer evaluations within the capstone team, and a completed portfolio.

What happens in the capstone?

The capstone runs over the final six months. Teams of four to six work with an external client to innovate, improve or modify a new or existing digital product or service, in areas such as education, the environment, health care and retail. Past clients listed on the website include the Discovery Cube museum, Monterey Bay Aquarium, Data for Social Good and Code.org, as well as many for-profit organisations. The website stresses that iterative research, design, development and evaluation are the keys to a successful capstone.

What are the entry requirements, and what TOEFL or IELTS score do you need?

  • Degree: a bachelor's degree from a regionally accredited US institution or the international equivalent; only four-year degrees are accepted, not three-year degrees.
  • GPA: a minimum of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale.
  • English: under UCI Graduate Division rules, a TOEFL score of at least 80 (or 4 on the new scale introduced in January 2026), or an Academic IELTS score of at least 7 overall with no band below 6. Scores must be less than two years old; the TOEFL institution code is 4859, and MyBest scores are not accepted. Applicants whose bachelor's or master's degree is from an institution where English was the sole language of instruction, according to the WHED database, are exempt.
  • Materials: the online application, a statement of purpose (why you want to join, how it fits your career and your future goals), a résumé, three letters of recommendation (the website notes these can, and often should, come from managers, peers or clients), unofficial transcripts from every college attended and either a portfolio or GRE scores (a portfolio is strongly recommended). A personal history statement is optional.

How should you prepare the portfolio?

The website says a qualified portfolio waives the GRE, and that it finds a portfolio a better indicator of how students will perform than a GRE score. The MHCID portfolio is not limited to design work; examples from any field count, as long as they show strong writing skills, familiarity with computers and technology, and strength in your current field.

  • Size: three or four pieces that best show your work; if you only have two or three strong projects, do not add weaker ones to fill space.
  • A summary page for each piece: describe the work, the skills used, the outcomes and your role.
  • Format: a custom website or a PDF. Website links go in your statement of purpose or résumé, and PDFs can be uploaded. Confidential work may be redacted (for example, a former employer's financial details).

How much does it cost, and can international students apply?

  • Fees: MHCID is a self-supporting professional programme. According to the UCI Registrar's schedule for the cohort entering in Fall 2026, the programme fee is US$59,940, plus a US$30 Student Services Access Fee each quarter: US$15,015 for each of four quarters (autumn, winter, spring and summer), or US$60,060 in total, with an optional US$7 UCGPC fee. The website says this covers all programme costs except travel to the three in-person sessions and books. Fees can change each year, so check the Registrar's latest schedule for 2027 entry.
  • Deposit and insurance: admitted students pay a US$500 Statement of Intent to Register deposit, applied to first-quarter fees on enrolment. Graduate student health insurance (GSHIP) is neither offered through the programme nor required.
  • Fellowships: the executive committee reviews every applicant for admission and for individual fellowships, and tries to announce fellowships with offers, though there can be delays. Because the programme is not state-supported, application fee waivers may not apply.
  • International students and visas: the programme welcomes international applicants and confirms that MHCID qualifies as a STEM degree, but because it is low-residency (no more than a week on campus at a time), it cannot issue I-20s and does not help students obtain a student visa. People already in the US on a non-student visa (for example, family or work) should generally be able to enrol, but the website advises checking with UCI's international centre and an immigration attorney. Applicants based outside the US who need to travel for the intensives should clarify entry and attendance arrangements before applying.

Where do graduates work?

Alumni roles listed on the website include UX designer, UX researcher, graphic designer, product designer, content designer, product manager, UX writer and UI accessibility engineer, at employers such as Google, Microsoft, Meta, Apple, Amazon, LinkedIn, Zoom, Oracle, Intel, Boeing, Medtronic, Johnson & Johnson and LEGO BrickLink. The programme also offers personalised academic advising and career support through workshops, coaching and networking events. Like all University of California master's degrees, MHCID is accredited by WSCUC.

How should you plan a 2027 application?

  • November 2026 to January 2027: first confirm that your visa status allows you to enrol (no I-20 is available); assemble three or four pieces with summary pages, and secure TOEFL 80 or IELTS 7 (bands of 6) or above.
  • February to April 2027: finish your statement of purpose and résumé and invite three recommenders (managers, peers or clients are fine). The website encourages you not to wait until the last minute.
  • 15 May 2027: the Fall 2027 application deadline.
  • Summer 2027: after admission, pay the US$500 deposit and start the pre-reading list as soon as it arrives; return to campus in early September for the IN4MATX 280 intensive.

How can design and architecture graduates prepare?

Author's advice (not an official requirement): MHCID values work experience and UX thinking rather than polished renderings. In 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, we have found that the most convincing work from spatial designers moving into UX takes a real design project and reframes it as a process: who the users are, how the problem was defined, what research was done and how the solution changed in response to feedback, with a summary page that states your role and outcomes. That maps directly onto the writing, technology and professional strengths the website asks for. If you need an F-1 visa to study full-time in the US, MHCID is not the right fit; compare our guides to CMU's MHCI, the University of Washington's MHCI+D, Georgia Tech's MS-HCI and CMU's ETC.

Official sources checked: MHCID home, about the programme, admissions, applicant portfolio, curriculum, capstone projects, career outcomes, FAQ, UCI 2026–27 catalogue, UCI Registrar MHCID fee schedule and UCI Graduate Division English requirements (checked October 2026).

q.zh-Hant: UCI MHCID 讀多久？學費多少？
q.en: How long is UCI's MHCID, and how much does it cost?

a.zh-Hant: 約 12 個月、48 學分，分秋、冬、春、夏四個學季。依 2026 年秋季入學的費用表，每學季 15,015 美元，合計 60,060 美元，不含回校三次的交通與書籍；費用每年可能調整。
a.en: About 12 months and 48 units across four quarters (autumn, winter, spring and summer). For the cohort entering in Fall 2026, fees are US$15,015 per quarter, or US$60,060 in total, excluding travel for the three campus visits and books; fees can change each year.

q.zh-Hant: 國際生可以用 MHCID 申請 F-1 學生簽證嗎？
q.en: Can international students use MHCID to obtain an F-1 student visa?

a.zh-Hant: 不行。官網說明因為是低駐校課程，無法簽發 I-20，也不協助辦理學生簽證。已持其他簽證在美國的人通常可以就讀，但官網建議先向 UCI 國際中心與移民律師確認。
a.en: No. The website says that because the programme is low-residency, it cannot issue I-20s or help with student visas. People already in the US on another visa can generally enrol, but the website advises checking with UCI's international centre and an immigration attorney first.

q.zh-Hant: 托福、雅思要多少分？要考 GRE 嗎？
q.en: What TOEFL or IELTS score is required, and is the GRE needed?

a.zh-Hant: TOEFL 至少 80，或 IELTS 至少 7 且單項不低於 6。GRE 與作品集二選一，官網強烈建議交作品集，並認為作品集比 GRE 更能預測表現。
a.en: TOEFL 80 or IELTS 7 with no band below 6. You submit either a portfolio or GRE scores; the website strongly recommends a portfolio and considers it a better predictor than the GRE.

q.zh-Hant: 作品集要放幾件？一定要是設計作品嗎？
q.en: How many pieces should the portfolio include, and must it be design work?

a.zh-Hant: 建議 3 到 4 件，不必是設計作品，任何工作領域的成果都可以，但每件都要附摘要頁，說明內容、技能、成果與你的角色；格式為個人網站或 PDF。
a.en: Three or four pieces are suggested, and they need not be design work; examples from any field count, but each needs a summary page covering the work, skills, outcomes and your role. Use a custom website or a PDF.

q.zh-Hant: 2027 入學什麼時候截止？要回校幾次？
q.en: When is the 2027 deadline, and how often must you be on campus?

a.zh-Hant: 只收秋季入學，2027 年秋季入學截止日是 2027 年 5 月 15 日。整年回爾灣校園三次：9 月初密集課、3 月下旬春季密集課與 Capstone 啟動、隔年 9 月畢業典禮。
a.en: Entry is in the autumn only, and the Fall 2027 deadline is 15 May 2027. Students visit the Irvine campus three times: an intensive in early September, a Spring Intensive and capstone kickoff in late March, and commencement the following September.

posts.abstract_en: A guide to UC Irvine's Master of Human-Computer Interaction and Design (MHCID), checked against official sources in October 2026. Offered by the Department of Informatics, it is a one-year, 48-unit, low-residency professional master's for working UX professionals, taught mostly online with three campus visits and a six-month industry capstone. It admits for the autumn only, with a 15 May 2027 deadline for Fall 2027, and requires a four-year bachelor's, a 3.0 GPA, TOEFL 80 or IELTS 7, and a portfolio or GRE scores. Fees for the Fall 2026 cohort total US$60,060. Although it is a STEM degree, the programme cannot issue I-20s, so it cannot be used for an F-1 student visa.

summary.zh-Hant: 卡內基美隆大學娛樂科技中心（ETC）的娛樂科技碩士是兩年、以團隊項目為核心的遊戲與互動娛樂碩士。對照官網整理沉浸學期與三個 14 週項目、作品集或 GRE、IELTS 每項 7／TOEFL 每項 23 的英文門檻、2 月 1 日材料期限與 3 月 15 日放榜、一年約 9.9 萬美元就學費用與 91% 一年內就業。
summary.en: Carnegie Mellon's Master of Entertainment Technology, offered by the Entertainment Technology Center (ETC), is a two-year, team-project master's in games and interactive entertainment. Checked against official sources: the Immersion Semester and three 14-week projects, portfolio or GRE, English minimums of IELTS 7 in every band or TOEFL 23 per section, the 1 February materials date and 15 March decisions, a cost of attendance of about US$99,000 a year and 91% employment within a year.

tldr.zh-Hant: CMU ETC 由計算機科學學院與美術學院合辦，Master of Entertainment Technology 為兩年四個全日制學期、不能提早畢業；第一學期四門必修（Building Virtual Worlds、Visual Story、Improvisational Acting、ETC Fundamentals），後三學期每學期一個 14 週團隊項目，常有外部客戶；申請要履歷、四題 250 字短文（禁用 AI）、作品集（4–8 件、須為網站）和／或 GRE、3 封推薦信、正式成績單、75 美元申請費與 Zoom 面試；英文 IELTS 7 且每項 7、TOEFL 舊制 92 每項 23（新制 5.0）、Duolingo 130；1 月 15 日後開始審查、2 月 1 日前材料送達、3 月 15 日放榜；2026–27 學費 61,628 美元、總就學費用 99,002 美元；成績獎學金平均每年約 1 萬美元；91% 畢業一年內就業、平均起薪 8 萬美元以上。
tldr.en: CMU's ETC is run jointly by the School of Computer Science and the College of Fine Arts. The Master of Entertainment Technology lasts two years (four full-time semesters) and cannot be finished early. The first semester has four required courses (Building Virtual Worlds, Visual Story, Improvisational Acting and ETC Fundamentals), followed by a 14-week team project in each of the next three semesters, often with external clients. Applicants submit a CV, four 250-word essays (no AI), a portfolio (4 to 8 pieces, as a website) and/or GRE, three letters, an official transcript and a US$75 fee, followed by a Zoom interview. English: IELTS 7 in every band, TOEFL 92 with 23 per section (5.0 on the new scale) or Duolingo 130. Review starts after 15 January, materials are due by 1 February and decisions come on 15 March. For 2026–27, tuition is US$61,628 and the total cost of attendance US$99,002; merit scholarships average about US$10k a year; 91% of graduates are employed within a year, with an average starting salary of US$80,000+.

body.zh-Hant:
結論先講：卡內基美隆大學（Carnegie Mellon University，CMU）的 Master of Entertainment Technology（MET，娛樂科技碩士）由娛樂科技中心（Entertainment Technology Center，ETC）開設，ETC 是 CMU 計算機科學學院與美術學院合辦的跨領域中心，位於匹茲堡。這是一個 兩年、四個全日制學期的專業碩士：第一學期是四門必修的「沉浸學期」，之後三個學期每學期做一個 14 週的團隊項目，做出能實際運作的遊戲、互動體驗或原型。申請時 作品集與 GRE 可二選一或都交，作品集必須是網站；英文要求偏高：IELTS 總分與每個單項都要 7、舊制 TOEFL 92 且每項 23（2026 年 1 月起的新制為總分與單項 5.0）、或 Duolingo 130。官網表示 1 月 15 日後開始審查，推薦信等材料須在 2 月 1 日前送達，3 月 15 日公布結果。依 CMU 學生財務處 2026–27 學年費用表，學費一年 61,628 美元，含生活費等的總就學費用約 99,002 美元。

以下內容於 2026 年 10 月對照 ETC 官網的介紹、學術、課程、設施、職涯、申請與學費頁，以及 CMU 學生財務處費用表查核。早期流傳的「GRE 建議 325 分」「雅思 7.5」等說法在官網查不到出處，已刪除或改為官網現行要求。

文首封面是 ETC 設施頁的主視覺：在霓虹燈光的展示艙中，一具復古機器人站在兩面圓窗螢幕之間。圖片來源：卡內基美隆大學 ETC 官網

CMU ETC 娛樂科技碩士是什麼？適合誰讀？

ETC 在 1999 年由計算機科學教授 Randy Pausch（《最後的演講》作者）與戲劇教授 Don Marinelli 創立，定位是藝術與科技交會的地方。官網說畢業生進入的產業包括遊戲、影視、主題樂園等實體娛樂、軟體開發、人工智慧，以及「還沒有名字的新領域」。

它不是傳統的研究型碩士，而是以 團隊做東西 為核心：學生來自電腦、工程、藝術、設計、戲劇、寫作等各種背景，官網直說「我們不再把申請者分成技術人或藝術家」。如果你喜歡跨領域合作、想做遊戲、互動裝置、XR、主題樂園體驗或教育遊戲，ETC 很對口；如果你想要一年讀完，或想邊工作邊讀，就不適合，官網說課程無法在兩年內提早完成，也強烈不建議在系外打工（系內助教等工作除外）。

兩年課程怎麼安排？要修哪些課？

  • 第一學期：沉浸學期（Immersion Semester）。四門必修課：Building Virtual Worlds（由 Randy Pausch 開創，跨背景組隊快速做出虛擬世界，學期末在年度最大活動 Fall Festival 展出）、Visual Story（學電影語言與導演手法，應用到遊戲、主題樂園與數位體驗）、Improvisational Acting（即興表演，用來練團隊信任與臨場反應）、ETC Fundamentals（建立娛樂科技的共同語彙，並開始經營業界人脈）。
  • 後三個學期：項目課。每學期換一個新項目，14 週內由跨領域團隊在教師指導下做出可運作的作品或可玩的原型；很多項目有外部客戶，例如企業、非營利組織或學區。項目可能是學生自己提案，也可能是為客戶解題。
  • 選修：第一學期後每學期選一門選修，可修 ETC 的課，也可修 CMU 其他學院的課。
  • 轉化遊戲（Transformational Play）方向：與 CMU 轉化遊戲中心合作的選讀方向，研究如何用遊戲解決真實問題；仍屬 ETC 主要班級，但有指定選修，且第一年與第二年之間必須做一個暑期項目。
  • 暑期：暑期實習為選擇性；學生也可在學期中參加合作實習（co-op）並取得學分。

有哪些設備？

官網說每位學生在兩年內都有一台專屬的高效能桌機（2025–26 學年為搭載 RTX 4080 Super 的 Lenovo Legion），配 32 吋 4K 與 27 吋雙螢幕，預裝 Maya、3ds Max、ZBrush、Houdini、Adobe 全套、Unity 6、Unreal Engine 5 等。共用設施包括：可模擬乘坐體驗的三面 CAVE 動感投影系統、270 度的 CAVERN、四人互動鼓桌 Jam-O-Drum、錄音室、綠幕攝影棚、道具與木工坊（3D 列印、雷射切割），以及 Unitree G1 人形機器人；VR／AR 頭顯、動作捕捉與 Arduino 等硬體也可借用。

申請條件是什麼？托福、雅思要多少？

  • 線上申請表與履歷：履歷要是最新版本，實習、工作、課程、畢業設計、個人項目只要和娛樂科技有關都可以寫。
  • 四題短文：放在同一份文件，每題不超過 250 字：你目前最強的技能與想在 ETC 學的技能、你的背景如何讓你準備好團隊合作、職涯目標與 ETC 的幫助、誰或什麼啟發了你。官網明說 不可用 ChatGPT 或任何 AI 工具生成。
  • 作品集和／或 GRE：可擇一或都交。GRE 須由 ETS 直接送分，代碼 2074。作品集放 4 到 8 件最能代表你的作品（傳統或數位藝術、平面設計、寫作、程式等，必要時可用照片或影片），團隊作品要寫明你負責的部分；必須以網站形式提交，Google Drive 連結不會被審閱。官網也接受非傳統作品集，例如提案書或商業計畫。
  • 3 封推薦信：來自能評估你學術或專業能力的教授、項目主管或雇主，朋友與同儕不行，須在 2 月 1 日前送達。
  • 英文（母語非英語者必交，不接受豁免）：TOEFL iBT 舊制（2026 年 1 月前考）總分 92、每項 23；新制（2026 年 1 月起）總分與每項 5.0；IELTS 總分 7.0 且每項 7；Duolingo 總分與每項 130。成績須在兩年內，送分代碼 2074。
  • 正式成績單：須由大學直接寄給 ETC（電子版優先），學生自行上傳的不算。
  • 申請費：75 美元，可申請減免。送件後會安排 Zoom 面試。

作品集要怎麼準備？

ETC 的作品集不是只看畫功。官網說作品集要放「最能展現你技能組合」的作品，可以是平面設計、傳統藝術、音樂、寫作或任何創作媒材；團隊項目要清楚說明你個人的貢獻。因為課程幾乎全是團隊項目，建議每件作品都交代：你的角色、團隊怎麼分工、做了幾輪測試與修改、最後成果能不能被玩或被體驗。可運作的遊戲 Demo、互動裝置影片、關卡或場景設計、角色與世界觀設定，都比單張漂亮的圖更有說服力。

學費多少？有獎學金嗎？

  • 學費：依 CMU 學生財務處 2026–27 學年 ETC 費用表，學費一年 61,628 美元（每學期 30,814 美元）；加上學生活動費 248 美元、科技費 490 美元、交通費 302 美元，以及住宿 14,752、餐費 8,664、書籍用品 2,212、健康保險 3,352、個人雜支 4,098、旅費 1,756 與預估貸款費 1,500 美元，一年總就學費用約 99,002 美元（2026 年 7 月 30 日版本）。兩年課程要準備兩個學年的費用，2027 年入學請以最新費用表為準。
  • 獎學金：所有申請者自動被考慮少量的成績獎學金，平均每年約 1 萬美元，先給一年、依成績可續第二年；另有 Schell Games 贊助的 ETC Fellowship Fund，提供第一年全額學費、成績良好可續第二年，需另外申請，優先考慮經濟或地域弱勢、單親家庭或家中第一代大學生。
  • 智慧財產：官網強調學生在 ETC 做出的作品，智慧財產權屬於學生本人。

畢業生去哪裡工作？

官網職涯頁列出的數字是：91% 畢業一年內就業、平均起薪 80,000 美元以上，2025 年有 30 次企業參訪。第一學期有必修的職涯發展課（履歷檢視、模擬面試、校友人脈），第一年春天全班會去洛杉磯與舊金山參加一週的西岸參訪（West Coast Trip），拜訪遊戲工作室、娛樂公司與設計公司。校友任職公司包括 Apple、Meta、Electronic Arts、Blizzard、Disney、Universal、Epic Games、Rockstar Games、Sony、Naughty Dog 等。

2027 申請時間線怎麼排？

  • 2026 年 11 月：確定英文成績路線（IELTS 每項 7 或 TOEFL 每項 23／新制 5.0 對很多人是門檻），聯絡 3 位推薦人；把作品集整理成網站。
  • 2026 年 12 月至 2027 年 1 月中：寫完四題短文（每題 250 字內、親自撰寫），完成申請表並繳費；請學校直接寄正式成績單。線上申請須在 2027/1/1 前送出。官網說 1 月 15 日後開始審查。
  • 2027 年 2 月 1 日：推薦信、成績單與官方考試成績的最後送達期限。
  • 2027 年 2 月至 3 月：Zoom 面試；3 月 15 日在申請系統公布結果。

設計、建築背景怎麼準備最有利？

作者建議（非官方要求）：建築與空間設計背景其實很適合 ETC 的主題樂園、沉浸式展覽、XR 場景與關卡設計方向。我們在 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢中看到，最有說服力的作品集通常會把一個空間設計項目延伸成「可體驗的敘事」：使用者怎麼移動、在哪裡被驚喜、互動怎麼觸發，再配上一兩件用 Unity 或 Unreal 做出的可玩原型或互動影片，並清楚標示團隊中的個人分工。如果你更想做產品與介面的 UX，可以比較我們整理的 CMU 人機交互碩士 MHCI、華盛頓大學 MHCI+D、喬治亞理工學院 MS-HCI 與 加州大學爾灣分校 MHCID。

官方查核來源：ETC 介紹、學術、課程、設施與技術、職涯服務、申請、學費與獎學金、CMU 學生財務處 2026–27 ETC 費用表（2026 年 10 月查核）。
body.en:
The short answer: Carnegie Mellon University's Master of Entertainment Technology (MET) is offered by the Entertainment Technology Center (ETC), a joint venture between CMU's School of Computer Science and College of Fine Arts, based in Pittsburgh. It is a two-year professional master's of four full-time semesters: the first is a four-course "Immersion Semester", and in each of the remaining three semesters students work in a team on a 14-week project to build a working game, interactive experience or prototype. Applicants submit a portfolio, GRE scores or both, and the portfolio must be a website. The English bar is high: IELTS 7 overall and in every band, TOEFL 92 with 23 in each section on the pre-2026 scale (5.0 overall and per section for tests taken from January 2026), or Duolingo 130. The ETC begins reviewing applications after 15 January, requires recommendations and other materials by 1 February and releases decisions on 15 March. Under CMU Student Financial Services' 2026–27 schedule, tuition is US$61,628 a year, and the total cost of attendance, including living costs, is about US$99,002.

Everything below was checked in October 2026 against the ETC website's about, academics, curriculum, facilities, career, admissions and tuition pages, and CMU Student Financial Services' fee schedule. Earlier claims in circulation, such as a "recommended GRE of 325" or "IELTS 7.5", could not be found on the official website and have been removed or replaced with current requirements.

The cover is the banner image from the ETC facilities page: a retro robot standing between two porthole screens in a neon-lit display pod. Image source: Carnegie Mellon ETC website

What is CMU's ETC master's, and who is it for?

The ETC was founded in 1999 by computer science professor Randy Pausch (of "The Last Lecture") and drama professor Don Marinelli, as the place where art and technology meet. The website says its graduates go into gaming, film and television, location-based entertainment, software development, artificial intelligence, and "something so new it doesn't have a category yet".

It is not a traditional research master's; its core is making things in teams. Students come from computing, engineering, art, design, drama, writing and more, and the website says it is no longer easy, or necessary, to sort applicants into technologists and artists. If you enjoy cross-disciplinary collaboration and want to make games, interactive installations, XR, theme-park experiences or educational games, the ETC is a strong match. If you want to finish in one year or work while studying, it is not: the website says the degree cannot be completed in less than two years and strongly discourages outside work (roles within the ETC, such as teaching assistant, are the exception).

How are the two years structured, and what do you study?

  • First semester: the Immersion Semester. Four required courses: Building Virtual Worlds (started by Randy Pausch, in which mixed-background teams rapidly build virtual worlds, shown at the year's biggest event, Fall Festival), Visual Story (the language of filmmaking and directing, applied to games, theme parks and digital experiences), Improvisational Acting (to build trust and the ability to react in the moment as a team) and ETC Fundamentals (a shared vocabulary for entertainment technology and a start on professional networks).
  • The remaining three semesters: project courses. A new project each semester, in which an interdisciplinary team supervised by faculty produces a working artefact or playable prototype in 14 weeks; many projects have external clients such as companies, nonprofits or school districts. Some projects are pitched by students; others solve a client's problem.
  • Electives: after the first semester, students take an elective each term, at the ETC or elsewhere at CMU.
  • Transformational Play concentration: an optional concentration with the Center for Transformational Play on designing playful systems that address real-world challenges. Students stay in the main ETC cohort but follow approved electives and must complete a summer project between years one and two.
  • Summers: a summer internship is optional; students can also take semester co-ops for academic credit.

What facilities are available?

According to the website, every student is assigned a personal high-performance desktop for the two years (a Lenovo Legion with an RTX 4080 Super GPU in 2025–26) with 32-inch 4K and 27-inch monitors, preloaded with Maya, 3ds Max, ZBrush, Houdini, the full Adobe suite, Unity 6, Unreal Engine 5 and more. Shared facilities include a three-wall CAVE with a pneumatic motion base for ride simulation, the 270-degree CAVERN, the four-player Jam-O-Drum interactive table, a sound studio, a green screen studio, a prop studio and woodshop (3D printers and a laser cutter) and a Unitree G1 humanoid robot; VR and AR headsets, motion capture and kits such as Arduino can be signed out.

What are the entry requirements, and what TOEFL or IELTS score do you need?

  • Online application and CV: use your most current CV; internships, jobs, coursework, thesis work and personal projects all count if they relate to entertainment technology.
  • Four short essays: in a single document, no more than 250 words each, on your strongest skills and what you want to learn at the ETC, how your background prepares you for teamwork, your career goals and how the ETC will help, and who or what inspires you. The website states that ChatGPT or any other AI tool must not be used to generate them.
  • Portfolio and/or GRE: submit either or both. GRE scores go directly from ETS using code 2074. A portfolio should hold 4 to 8 pieces that best show your skills (traditional or digital art, graphic design, writing, coding and so on, with photos or video where needed), and group pieces need a note on what you did; it must be submitted as a website, and Google Drive portfolios are not reviewed. Non-traditional portfolios, such as a grant proposal or business plan, are also welcome.
  • Three letters of recommendation: from professors, project directors or employers who can assess your academic or professional work (not friends or peers), received by 1 February.
  • English (required for non-native speakers, with no exceptions): TOEFL iBT taken before January 2026, 92 overall with 23 in each section; taken from January 2026, 5.0 overall and in each section; IELTS 7.0 overall and 7 in each band; or Duolingo 130 overall and in each subscore. Scores must be under two years old, sent with code 2074.
  • Official transcript: sent directly to the ETC by your university (electronic preferred); student uploads are not accepted.
  • Application fee: US$75, with waivers available on request. Zoom interviews are held after you apply.

How should you prepare the portfolio?

The ETC portfolio is not only about drawing skill. The website asks for the work that best demonstrates your skill set, in graphic design, traditional art, music, writing or any creative medium, and wants group projects to explain your own contribution. Because the programme is almost entirely team-based, it helps for every piece to show your role, how the team divided the work, how many rounds of testing and revision you did and whether the result can be played or experienced. A working game demo, a video of an interactive installation, level or environment design, or character and world-building work is more convincing than a single beautiful image.

How much does it cost, and are there scholarships?

  • Tuition: under CMU Student Financial Services' 2026–27 ETC schedule, tuition is US$61,628 a year (US$30,814 per semester). Adding the student activities fee (US$248), technology fee (US$490) and transportation fee (US$302), plus housing (14,752), food (8,664), books and supplies (2,212), health insurance (3,352), personal costs (4,098), travel (1,756) and estimated loan fees (1,500), the total cost of attendance is about US$99,002 a year (version of 30 July 2026). Budget for two academic years, and check the latest schedule for 2027 entry.
  • Scholarships: every applicant is automatically considered for a limited number of merit scholarships, averaging about US$10k a year, granted for one year and renewable for the second on academic performance. The ETC Fellowship Fund, sponsored by Schell Games, covers full tuition for the first year, renewable for the second in good standing; it requires a separate application and prefers students from under-privileged socioeconomic backgrounds or underrepresented areas, single-parent households or first-generation college students.
  • Intellectual property: the website stresses that the IP of what students make at the ETC belongs to the students.

Where do graduates work?

The career page reports 91% employed within a year of graduation and an average starting salary of US$80,000+, with 30 company visits in 2025. The first semester includes a required professional development course (CV reviews, mock interviews and alumni networking), and each spring the first-year cohort spends a week on the West Coast Trip in Los Angeles and San Francisco, visiting game studios, entertainment firms and design agencies. Alumni work at companies including Apple, Meta, Electronic Arts, Blizzard, Disney, Universal, Epic Games, Rockstar Games, Sony and Naughty Dog.

How should you plan a 2027 application?

  • November 2026: settle your English test route (IELTS 7 in every band or TOEFL 23 per section, or 5.0 on the new scale, is the hurdle for many), contact three recommenders and build your portfolio website.
  • December 2026 to mid-January 2027: finish the four essays (250 words each, written yourself), complete the application and pay the fee, and ask your university to send an official transcript. The online application must be submitted by Jan 1, 2027. The website says review begins after 15 January.
  • 1 February 2027: the final date for recommendations, transcripts and official test scores.
  • February to March 2027: Zoom interviews, with decisions released in the portal on 15 March.

How can design and architecture graduates prepare?

Author's advice (not an official requirement): architecture and spatial design graduates are a natural fit for the ETC's theme-park, immersive exhibition, XR environment and level design directions. In 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, we have found that the most convincing portfolios extend a spatial design project into an experience-driven narrative: how people move, where they are surprised and how interactions are triggered, backed by one or two playable prototypes or interaction videos made in Unity or Unreal, with your role in the team clearly labelled. If you are more interested in product and interface UX, compare our guides to CMU's MHCI, the University of Washington's MHCI+D, Georgia Tech's MS-HCI and UC Irvine's MHCID.

Official sources checked: about the ETC, academics, curriculum, facilities and technology, career services, admissions, tuition and financial aid and CMU Student Financial Services 2026–27 ETC cost of attendance (checked October 2026).

q.zh-Hant: CMU ETC 讀多久？可以一年讀完或邊工作邊讀嗎？
q.en: How long is CMU's ETC master's, and can you finish in one year or work while studying?

a.zh-Hant: 兩年、四個全日制學期，官網說無法在兩年內提早完成；暑期實習為選擇性。因為課業量大，官網強烈不建議在系外工作，但學生常在 ETC 內擔任助教等職位。
a.en: Two years, or four full-time semesters, and the website says it cannot be completed in less than two years; a summer internship is optional. Because of the workload, the website strongly discourages working outside the department, though students often work as TAs or in other ETC roles.

q.zh-Hant: 托福、雅思要多少分？
q.en: What TOEFL or IELTS score is required?

a.zh-Hant: IELTS 總分 7.0 且每項 7；TOEFL iBT 2026 年 1 月前考的要總分 92、每項 23，2026 年 1 月起的新制要總分與每項 5.0；或 Duolingo 總分與每項 130。母語非英語者必交，不接受豁免，成績須在兩年內。
a.en: IELTS 7.0 overall and 7 in every band; TOEFL iBT taken before January 2026, 92 overall with 23 per section, or 5.0 overall and per section from January 2026; or Duolingo 130 overall and per subscore. Non-native speakers must submit a test, with no exceptions, and scores must be under two years old.

q.zh-Hant: 一定要交作品集嗎？要考 GRE 嗎？
q.en: Is a portfolio required, and do you need the GRE?

a.zh-Hant: 作品集與 GRE 至少交一項，也可以都交。作品集放 4 到 8 件，必須是網站形式，Google Drive 不會被審閱；團隊作品要寫明個人貢獻，也接受提案書等非傳統作品集。
a.en: Submit at least one of a portfolio or GRE scores, or both. A portfolio should have 4 to 8 pieces and must be a website (Google Drive portfolios are not reviewed); group work needs a note on your contribution, and non-traditional portfolios such as proposals are welcome.

q.zh-Hant: CMU ETC 學費多少？有獎學金嗎？
q.en: How much does the CMU ETC cost, and are there scholarships?

a.zh-Hant: 2026–27 學年學費 61,628 美元，含住宿、餐費、保險等的總就學費用約 99,002 美元，讀兩年要準備兩年費用。所有申請者自動被考慮成績獎學金（平均每年約 1 萬美元），另有需另行申請、第一年全額學費的 ETC Fellowship Fund。
a.en: For 2026–27, tuition is US$61,628 and the total cost of attendance, including housing, food and insurance, is about US$99,002, so budget for two years. All applicants are automatically considered for merit scholarships (about US$10k a year on average), and the separately applied-for ETC Fellowship Fund covers first-year tuition in full.

q.zh-Hant: 什麼時候截止、什麼時候放榜？
q.en: When are the deadlines and decisions?

a.zh-Hant: 官網說 1 月 15 日後開始審查，推薦信、成績單與考試成績須在 2 月 1 日前送達，送件後安排 Zoom 面試，3 月 15 日在申請系統公布結果。線上申請須在 2027/1/1 前送出。
a.en: The website says review begins after 15 January, recommendations, transcripts and test scores are due by 1 February, Zoom interviews follow submission and decisions are released in the portal on 15 March. The online application must be submitted by Jan 1, 2027.

tldr.zh-Hant: UMSI MSI 兩年 48 學分、五條 pathway；UX／HCI 走 User Experience Research and Design，以 SI 699 收尾，另需 6 學分實習。不需 GRE；國際生 1/15 截止（亦為獎學金優先日）；材料含成績單、3 推薦、250 字短文、1–2 頁個人陳述、履歷，作品集選交；英文建議 TOEFL 舊制 102／每項 25（新制 5.0）或雅思 7.5。2026–27 州外每學期學費 31,555 美元、四學期約 126,220 美元。2025 畢業生平均年薪約 91,000 美元（私部門約 95,000），就業率 88%。

body.zh-Hant:
結論先講：密西根大學安娜堡分校（University of Michigan–Ann Arbor）資訊學院（School of Information，UMSI）的 Master of Science in Information（MSI，資訊理學碩士）是兩年、48 學分的專業碩士。若你想走人機交互／UX，官網現行路徑名稱是 User Experience Research and Design（使用者體驗研究與設計），屬 MSI 五條 pathway 之一；早期資料常寫的「HCI specialization」已改為這條 UX 路徑。申請不需 GRE，國際生截止日是 1 月 15 日（也是獎學金優先審查日），英文建議舊制 TOEFL 102＋每項 25（新制 5.0＋每項 5.0）或雅思 7.5。2026–27 學年州外全日制學費每學期 31,555 美元，讀滿四學期約 126,220 美元（另加雜費）。2025 年畢業生就業報告：整體平均年薪約 91,000 美元、私部門約 95,000 美元、就業率 88%、工作滿意度 90%。

以下內容於 2026 年 10 月對照 UMSI 的 MSI 介紹、課程、UX 路徑、申請、學費、實習與 2026 就業報告，以及 CSE 設施頁查核。原文流傳的「四題各 250 字短文」「學費約 84,164 美元」等說法已過時或與官網不符，已刪除或改為現行規定。

文首封面是 Leinweber 電腦科學與資訊大樓外觀：UMSI 自 2025 年 5 月起的主要基地，位於 Ann Arbor 北校區。圖片來源：密西根大學資訊學院官網

密西根 MSI 的 UX／HCI 方向是什麼？適合誰讀？

MSI 培養用資訊與技術解決人、組織與社會問題的人，官網舉例可做介面設計、軟體、數位典藏或大尺度資料建模，並強調在有益處時使用 AI。學位結構是 48 學分（至少 39 學分須為資訊學院課程），多數人兩年讀完，也可三年到四年兼讀。

五條 pathway 分別是：資訊與資料分析、圖書館／檔案與知識環境、產品管理、以使用者為中心的應用開發，以及 User Experience Research and Design。選 UX 路徑的人，最後要以 mastery 課 SI 699 完成一個完整的使用者研究與設計項目。官網說申請者來自商管、工程、教育、法律、人文、社科與健康科學等多元背景；不設先修課、不要求 GRE。

UX Research and Design 路徑要修什麼？

  • 核心課（第一學期）：SI 500 Problem-Solving with People, Information, and Technology；SI 506 Programming I。
  • Mastery 先修：官網 UX 路徑頁列出 SI 582 Introduction to Interaction Design、SI 658 Information Architecture、SI 622 Needs Assessment and Usability Evaluation；另需從 methods 與 theories 清單各選修若干門（例如平面與視覺傳達、響應式無障礙網頁、使用者體驗原則、無障礙設計、AR／VR 應用等，以你入學屆別的修課表為準）。
  • Mastery 課：SI 699 UX Research and Design——一學期獨立或小組項目，從頭定義問題、做使用者研究、提案與原型、評估並向利害關係人溝通；過去主題例如無障礙、博物館展覽、經濟發展支援。
  • Selective：從進階使用者研究、資訊視覺化、進階平面、行動／AR／VR 體驗、UX＋開發＋PM 協作實驗室等清單選兩門。
  • 選修 9 學分：可跨 UMSI 其他路徑、其他學院，或拿去算實習學分。
  • 實習（必修）：須取得 6 學分實習（最多可到 9 學分），通常在第一年與第二年之間的暑假；須先完成兩學期課業才有資格拿實習學分。國際生在學業良好時，可透過 CPT 取得實習工作授權。

申請條件是什麼？托福、雅思要多少？

  • 學歷：認可院校學士（或國際同等學歷）；GPA 建議 3.0／4.0，低於 3.0 仍可能依整體材料錄取。
  • 申請費：美國公民／永久居民 75 美元；國際生 90 美元。
  • 成績單：先上傳非正式成績單；錄取後再交正式成績單。
  • 3 封推薦信：能實質評估你學術或專業能力的教授、雇主或志願服務主管；親友不行。
  • 短文（≤250 字）：描述一個你在資訊領域想探索的挑戰或機會，為什麼重要，以及 UMSI 研究所如何幫你投入。
  • 個人陳述（1–2 頁、雙倍行距）：說明為何讀 UMSI、學術／專業／個人準備、未來目標，以及你能為社群帶來什麼。
  • 履歷：必交。作品集非必交；若要交，把連結放在 Additional Information。
  • 英文（母語非英語者）：須交兩年內的 TOEFL 或 IELTS（接受居家／線上版）。官網建議：新制 TOEFL 總分與每項 5.0＋（舊制 102＋、每項 25＋），IELTS 總分 7.5＋；TOEFL 機構代碼 1839，系所代碼可填 99。若整個學位都在全英語授課學校完成、或為現任 U-M 學生等，可符合豁免條件（美國公民身分本身不自動豁免）。
  • 國際生：申請時不必先交財力證明；錄取後再依 I-20／F-1 指引補交。

學費多少？有獎學金嗎？

  • 2026–27 學費：密西根居民每學期 15,653 美元；州外／國際生全日制（≥9 學分）每學期 31,555 美元，另加雜費。多數人四學期讀完，州外學費合計約 126,220 美元；學費有封頂，同一學期多修學分不另加學費。
  • 獎學金：申請時自動納入 merit-based、need-informed 獎學金審查（部分到全額學費），1 月 15 日前提交可獲優先考慮；另有外部獎學金匹配最高 1 萬美元、GSI 助教等機會。

畢業生去哪裡？薪資如何？

依 2026 MSI Employment Report（調查 2025 年畢業生）：整體平均年薪約 91,000 美元（私部門約 95,000、公部門／非營利約 64,000），就業率 88%，工作滿意度 90%；科技業平均約 103,000 美元。雇主例子包括 University of Michigan、Michigan Medicine、Accenture、Microsoft、Amazon、Epic、JPMorgan Chase、Adobe、Alibaba、Stellantis 等。97% 畢業生認為實習對就業結果重要；約 20% 接受實習回流錄取。

2027 秋季申請時間線怎麼排？

  • 現在至 2026 年 12 月：準備 TOEFL／IELTS（瞄準舊制 102／每項 25 或新制 5.0，或雅思 7.5）、聯絡 3 位推薦人、整理履歷與可選作品集連結。
  • 國際生硬截止：2027 年 1 月 15 日。同時也是獎學金優先日；過後國內生仍可申請至 3 月 1 日，但仍建議趕 1 月 15 日。
  • 錄取後：依信函辦理 I-20 與財力文件；確認修課表上的 UX 先修與 SI 699 時程，並規劃第二年暑假前的實習。

設計、建築背景怎麼準備最有利？

作者建議（非官方要求）：MSI 的 UX 路徑不要求程式本科，但 SI 506 與互動設計課會用到基礎實作；建築／設計背景可把空間敘事、使用者動線與原型迭代寫進個人陳述，並在 Additional Information 放上作品集網站。我們在 12,000+ 小時設計教學與設計諮詢中看到，最有說服力的材料通常會交代：你如何定義問題、找了哪些使用者、做了幾輪測試，以及你個人在團隊項目中的決策。若你更想讀一年制、強項目的 HCI 碩士，可比較 CMU MHCI、華盛頓大學 MHCI+D、喬治亞理工 MS-HCI 與 UC Irvine MHCID。

官方查核來源：MSI 介紹、課程結構、UX Research and Design 路徑、申請說明、學費與獎助、實習要求、2026 MSI 就業報告、前往 UMSI／Leinweber、CSE 設施（Leinweber／Beyster）（2026 年 10 月查核）。
body.en:
The short answer: The University of Michigan–Ann Arbor School of Information (UMSI) offers a two-year, 48-credit Master of Science in Information (MSI). For human–computer interaction and UX, the current official pathway is User Experience Research and Design—one of five MSI pathways; older references to an "HCI specialization" map to this UX path. No GRE is required. International applicants face a 15 January deadline (also the priority date for UMSI scholarships). Recommended English scores are TOEFL 102+ with 25+ per section on the legacy scale (5.0+ overall and per section on the new scale) or IELTS 7.5+. For 2026–27, out-of-state full-time tuition is US$31,555 per term, or about US$126,220 over four terms, plus fees. The 2026 MSI Employment Report (2025 graduates) cites average salaries of about US$91,000 overall and US$95,000 in the private sector, an 88% employment rate and 90% job satisfaction.

Everything below was checked in October 2026 against UMSI's MSI overview, curriculum, UX pathway, admissions, tuition, internship and 2026 employment pages, plus the CSE facilities page. Earlier claims such as "four 250-word short essays" or "tuition of about US$84,164" are outdated or unsupported and have been removed or replaced.

The cover shows the Leinweber Computer Science and Information Building, UMSI's main home on North Campus since May 2025. Image source: University of Michigan School of Information website

What is Michigan's MSI UX / HCI path, and who is it for?

The MSI prepares students to solve problems for people, organizations and society with information and technology—user interfaces, software, digital collections or large-scale data, including applying AI where it helps. The degree is 48 graduate credits (at least 39 from UMSI courses). Most students finish in two years; part-time study over three to four years is also possible.

The five pathways are Information and Data Analytics; Libraries, Archives and Knowledge Environments in Society; Product Management; User-Centered Application Development; and User Experience Research and Design. UX pathway students cap their degree with the SI 699 mastery course. Applicants come from many fields; there are no prerequisite courses and no GRE.

What do you study on the UX Research and Design pathway?

  • Core (first semester): SI 500 and SI 506 Programming I.
  • Mastery prerequisites: the UX pathway page lists SI 582, SI 658 and SI 622, plus methods and theories electives (for example graphic/visual communication, responsive accessible web design, UX principles, accessibility, AR/VR). Confirm the sheet for your cohort.
  • Mastery course: SI 699 UX Research and Design—a semester-long project that defines a problem, researches users, prototypes and evaluates a solution.
  • Selectives: two courses from advanced user research, information visualization, mobile/AR/VR experiences, UX+dev+PM collaboration labs and related options.
  • Nine elective credits from other pathways, other U-M schools or internship courses.
  • Internship (required): six credits (up to nine), usually in the summer between years one and two, after two semesters of coursework. International students in good standing may use CPT.

What are the entry requirements, and what TOEFL or IELTS score do you need?

  • Degree: bachelor's or international equivalent; GPA of 3.0/4.0 recommended (below 3.0 still possible).
  • Fee: US$75 (US citizens/permanent residents) or US$90 (international).
  • Transcripts: unofficial at apply; official after admission.
  • Three recommendations from people who know your academic or professional work.
  • Short essay (≤250 words) on a challenge or opportunity in information you care about.
  • Personal statement (1–2 pages, double-spaced) on why UMSI, your preparation, goals and contribution.
  • Resume required. A portfolio is optional—add a link under Additional Information.
  • English: TOEFL or IELTS within two years. Recommended: new TOEFL 5.0+ overall and per section (legacy 102+ with 25+), or IELTS 7.5+. Institution code 1839. Waivers exist for full English-medium degrees or current U-M students; US citizenship alone does not waive the requirement.
  • International applicants do not submit financial documents until after admission for the I-20.

How much does it cost, and are there scholarships?

  • 2026–27 tuition: US$15,653 per term for Michigan residents; US$31,555 per full-time term for out-of-state students, plus fees—about US$126,220 in tuition over four terms. Tuition is capped per term, so extra credits that term do not cost more.
  • Scholarships: automatic consideration for merit-based, need-informed awards (partial to full tuition); apply by 15 January for first consideration. Matching funds up to US$10k for external scholarships and GSI roles are also described on the funding page.

Where do graduates work, and what do they earn?

The 2026 MSI Employment Report (2025 graduates) lists average salaries of about US$91,000 overall (about 95,000 private sector; 64,000 public/nonprofit), an 88% employment rate and 90% job satisfaction; technology averages about US$103,000. Employers include the University of Michigan, Michigan Medicine, Accenture, Microsoft, Amazon, Epic, JPMorgan Chase, Adobe, Alibaba and Stellantis. Ninety-seven percent of graduates said internships mattered for their outcome; about 20% accepted return offers.

How should you plan a Fall 2027 application?

  • Now through December 2026: book English tests, contact three recommenders and prepare your resume and optional portfolio link.
  • Hard deadline for international applicants: 15 January 2027—also the scholarship priority date. Domestic applicants may continue to 1 March, but 15 January is still wiser.
  • After admission: complete I-20 finances, map UX prerequisites toward SI 699 and plan the required internship.

How can design and architecture graduates prepare?

Author's advice (not an official requirement): the UX pathway does not require an undergraduate CS degree, but SI 506 and interaction courses expect basic making skills. Use your personal statement to connect spatial storytelling, user journeys and iterative prototyping, and put a portfolio URL in Additional Information. In 12,000+ hours of design teaching and design consulting, we have found that strong applications show how you framed a problem, whom you studied, how many test rounds you ran and what you personally decided in team work. For one-year, studio-heavy HCI master's options, compare CMU's MHCI, the University of Washington's MHCI+D, Georgia Tech's MS-HCI and UC Irvine's MHCID.

Official sources checked: MSI overview, curriculum, UX Research and Design pathway, how to apply, tuition and funding, internship requirement, 2026 MSI Employment Report, getting to UMSI / Leinweber and CSE facilities (Leinweber / Beyster) (checked October 2026).

keywords: 人機交互 碩士 學費

q.zh-Hant: MSI 還有叫 HCI specialization 的項目嗎？
q.en: Does MSI still offer an HCI specialization?

a.zh-Hant: 官網現行是五條 pathway，人機交互／UX 對應 User Experience Research and Design；早期「HCI specialization」名稱已改為這條 UX 路徑，請以申請當年度課程頁為準。
a.en: UMSI now lists five pathways; HCI/UX maps to User Experience Research and Design. Older “HCI specialization” wording refers to this UX path—confirm on the current curriculum pages.

q.zh-Hant: 托福、雅思要多少？一定要考嗎？
q.en: What TOEFL or IELTS score is needed, and is a test required?

a.zh-Hant: 母語非英語者原則上要交兩年內 TOEFL 或 IELTS。官網建議新制 TOEFL 總分與每項 5.0＋（舊制 102＋、每項 25＋），或雅思 7.5＋。全英語授課學位等情況可申請豁免。
a.en: Non-native speakers generally submit TOEFL or IELTS within two years. Recommended: new TOEFL 5.0+ overall and per section (legacy 102+ with 25+), or IELTS 7.5+. Waivers exist for full English-medium degrees and similar cases.

q.zh-Hant: 一定要交作品集嗎？要考 GRE 嗎？
q.en: Is a portfolio required, and is the GRE required?

a.zh-Hant: GRE 不要求。作品集非必交；若要交，把連結放在 Additional Information。履歷、短文與個人陳述則是必交。
a.en: No GRE. A portfolio is optional—add a link under Additional Information. A resume, short essay and personal statement are required.

q.zh-Hant: 一定要實習嗎？讀多久？

a.en: Yes—six internship credits (up to nine), usually the summer between years, after two semesters. Most students finish in two years; part-time over three to four years is allowed.
